subject: Fast-path Priority Failover — amendment request & proposed compromise
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-payments.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fast-path failover: RTO 5m ask & evidence request

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for last week’s architecture review. We’re getting final sign-off from Ops and Legal and need to lock the failover commitments in the SOW amendment. For high-value transaction flows (payment auths + settlement queue) Acme is requesting a guaranteed "fast-path" failover RTO of 5 minutes across our primary regions (US-East and eu-west). Our concerns: DNS TTLs, cache warmup for KV-backed sessions, and the coordination window for marketplace partners.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 5-minute RTO for the fast-path in both regions, and if not, what the measurable alternative would be? Legal also asked for:
- RPO target for the fast-path (seconds/minutes)
- A summary of the observable signals and reporting cadence (how you measure failover time)
- Any credits or financial remedy model if the commitment is missed

I’ve attached our question matrix (acme-FastPath-SLA-questions.pdf) with examples and an expected acceptance criteria table. We’re aiming to include an amendment into the renewal contract next week, so a concrete proposal by EOD Friday would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Jared
Jared Mills
PM, Reliability & Integrations — Acme Payments

Attachment: acme-FastPath-SLA-questions.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fast-path failover: RTO 5m ask & evidence request

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear matrix. Looping in Aditya and Marcus for the infra details; Karthik will help with the contract amendment language.

Short answer: a hard 5-minute across both regions is materially challenging for hosted customers without a dedicated priority lane because of DNS propagation, cross-region cache repopulation, and downstream partner handoffs. That said, we can offer a structured, transparent alternative:

Proposal (high level):
- Priority Failover Lane (opt-in addendum) for fast-path traffic that gets accelerated routing and pre-warmed KV snapshots.
- Targeted RTO: 12 minutes for US-East, 15–20 minutes for eu-west on hosted customers; 5 minutes achievable for Dedicated customers with a warm-standby and DNS pre-seeding.
- RPO: 5 minutes (continuous KV checkpointing + bounded commit window)
- Reporting: automated failover telemetry (start/end timestamps + root-cause tags) with a daily digest during the first 30 days after any event and monthly SLA reports thereafter.

I’m attaching a short draft amendment and an executive runbook summary for the approach (redwood-proposed-amendment-v1.pdf, fastpath-runbook-exec-summary.docx). If that compromise is acceptable, we’ll route the amendment through your legal and a DocuSign link.

Action items:
1) Aditya / Marcus: please add a concise technical note on expected failure modes and achievable timelines.
2) Jared: let us know whether Acme can opt for the Priority Failover Lane (addendum will include pricing and commit).
3) Karthik: will prepare contract language and credit calculation options.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-09-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fast-path failover: RTO 5m ask & evidence request

Jared / team — quick technical assessment from infra:

Summary of constraints:
- DNS TTL + global resolver caches: even with aggressive TTLs we expect 30–90s of propagation variability depending on upstream resolvers. DNS pre-seeding (via delegated glue records + health-check based routing) cuts time but doesn’t eliminate it.
- KV cache and session state: warm replicas and KV snapshot shipping reduce repopulation to low-single-digit minutes, but write buffers & in-flight transactions need bounded replay (that’s the RPO window).
- Marketplace and partner handshakes (webhooks, payment gateways): many partners accept only their own retries/backoff and can add unpredictable latency; for true 5-minute end-to-end we need partner-side SLAs too.

Practical compromise we can commit to for hosted:
- Implement Priority Failover Lane for fast-path traffic with pre-warmed KV snapshots and prioritized batching.
- Observed median failover completion (internal tests): ~9–11 minutes in US regions, ~12–16 minutes in eu-west under nominal load. 95th percentile extends ~+6 minutes in complex dependency graphs.
- Proposed contractual targets (hosted): RTO 12 minutes (US), RTO 15 minutes (EU), RPO 5 minutes; credits scale if observed event exceeds 2x target in critical flows.

For Dedicated customers with a warm-standby and DNS pre-seeding we can certify 5-minute RTO for the fast-path (subject to a non-disruptive failover drill every quarter and a small reserved capacity commitment).

I’ll attach a short tech note to the amendment covering measurement points (BGP/DNS handoff time, failover start timestamp, KV restore complete timestamp, application readiness timestamp).

— Aditya
VP, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Varga <elena.varga@fintrust.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fast-path failover: RTO 5m ask & evidence request

Sofia / Jared — on behalf of Acme Legal: thanks for the quick assessment. A few items from our side before we move to signature: 

1) Acme can accept the Hosted compromise if Redwood includes:
   - SLAs split by region (US: 12m, EU: 15m) with a defined measurement methodology;
   - Financial remedy schedule: pro-rated credits starting at the first missed event, with an annual cap (we propose 20% of fast-path fees).
2) Reporting cadence must be: immediate incident notification, detailed event report within 48 hours, and a post-incident RCA within 10 business days.
3) We need proof points: past test runs or a 1-hour live failover drill with telemetry that demonstrates <=15m completion in eu-west. Can Redwood commit to a runbook drill window in the next 30 days?

If Redwood agrees to the above, Legal will be prepared to sign the amendment and accept the Priority Failover Lane pricing. We’ll also want the DocuSign link and the HubSpot amendment record.

Regards,
Elena Varga
Sr. Counsel, FinTrust (on behalf of Acme Payments)
